about: Rules of tuneup.ps1 -Startup (design, sections 15.4 and 15.5). Each pattern is a .NET regular expression, tried without case on the name of an entry, its publisher, the file name of its program and its key. protect: shown, never turned off. recommend: marked recommended, never turned off on its own; wingetId only gives the uninstall command that is shown, never run; workApp: not recommended on a work PC (managed or joined to Entra ID). Every rule says why. The first rule that matches wins, so the specific ones go first.

protect.why: Microsoft Defender and Windows Security: the protection of Windows itself (some of its programs live outside the folder of Windows).

protect.pattern: \b(Malwarebytes|ESET|Kaspersky|Bitdefender|Avast|AVG|Norton|NortonLifeLock|Gen Digital|McAfee|Sophos|Trend Micro|CrowdStrike|SentinelOne|Webroot|F-Secure|WithSecure|Panda Security|G DATA|Avira|Cylance|Carbon Black|Cisco Secure Endpoint|Emsisoft|Comodo|ZoneAlarm)\b
protect.why: Antivirus and endpoint protection of other publishers: turned off at startup, the PC starts unprotected.

protect.pattern: \b(Cisco AnyConnect|Cisco Secure Client|GlobalProtect|PanGPA|PanGPS|Palo Alto Networks|FortiClient|Fortinet|OpenVPN|WireGuard|NordVPN|ExpressVPN|Proton ?VPN|Surfshark|Check Point|Zscaler|Pulse Secure|Ivanti|SonicWall|Tailscale|Cloudflare WARP)\b
protect.why: VPN clients: without them the PC cannot reach the network of the organization, or sends traffic outside the tunnel.
Control and enhancement services of the audio driver: without them jack detection, the microphone or the speaker tuning can stop working.
Touchpad helpers of the driver: gestures, scrolling and palm rejection.
Fn keys of laptops: brightness, volume, airplane mode, keyboard light and their on-screen indicators.

protect.pattern: \b(NVDisplay\.Container\w*|NVIDIA Display Container LS|igfxCUIService\w*|igfxEM|Intel\(R\) HD Graphics Control Panel Service|AMD External Events Utility|AUEPLauncher|WTabletServicePro|WTabletServiceCon|Wacom Professional Service|Wacom Consumer Service)\b
protect.why: Services of the display and pen drivers: display modes, color, hotplug and pen input. The companion apps of the same vendors are not here: they are recommend rules (companion-app).

protect.pattern: \b(GoogleUpdate\w*|Google Update\w*|GoogleChromeElevationService|MicrosoftEdgeUpdate\w*|Microsoft Edge Update\w*|MicrosoftEdgeElevationService|MozillaMaintenance|Mozilla Maintenance Service|Firefox Background Update|BraveUpdate\w*|Brave Update\w*|BraveSoftware Update|BraveElevationService|ClickToRunSvc|OfficeClickToRun|Office Automatic Updates( 2\.0)?|Microsoft Office Click-to-Run Service)\b
protect.why: Updaters of browsers and of Office: protected even though they are updaters, because without them the browser and Office get no security patches (the same principle as Windows Update in the blacklist).

The same updaters by their service name; anchored, so the browser itself (brave.exe) is not taken for its updater. The first service of Brave is named just brave, which is also the name of the browser and its Run entry: it is protected by its display name (Brave Update Service), in the rule above.

recommend.why: Steam opens at sign-in only to be ready; games start it when they need it. Anchored: steamwebhelper and other names with steam are not it.
Epic Games Launcher: a game launcher that waits in the background.
EA app: a game launcher that waits in the background.
Battle.net: a game launcher that waits in the background.
Ubisoft Connect: a game launcher that waits in the background.
GOG Galaxy: a game launcher that waits in the background.
Riot Client: a game launcher that waits in the background (Vanguard, the anti-cheat driver, is a driver and stays).
OneDrive syncs files in the background; on a PC of an organization it usually keeps the work files, so it is not recommended there.
Dropbox syncs in the background; it can be opened when it is needed.
Google Drive syncs in the background; it can be opened when it is needed.
MEGAsync syncs in the background; it can be opened when it is needed.
iCloud syncs in the background; it can be opened when it is needed.
Nextcloud syncs in the background; it can be opened when it is needed.
Discord opens at sign-in through its Update.exe; this rule goes before updater so it is not taken for an updater.
Teams opens at sign-in; on a PC of an organization it is how people are reached for meetings, so it is not recommended there.
The new Outlook can open at sign-in to check mail; on a PC of an organization it is the work mail, so it is not recommended there.
Skype opens at sign-in to be reachable.
Slack opens at sign-in to be reachable.
Zoom opens at sign-in; meetings start it when they need it.
Telegram opens at sign-in to be reachable.
WhatsApp opens at sign-in to be reachable.
NVIDIA companion apps: overlay, recording and driver downloads; the display driver works without them.
AMD Software Adrenalin: overlay, recording and driver downloads; the display driver works without it.
ASUS Armoury Crate: lighting, profiles and its own updater; the Fn keys are ATKOSD2 and HControlUser, which stay.
Logitech G HUB and Options+: profiles, lighting and custom buttons; mice and keyboards work with their default buttons without them.
Razer Synapse, Corsair iCUE and SteelSeries GG: lighting, macros and their own updaters.
Intel helpers: driver download checks and the graphics control panel; the drivers work without them.
Updaters of other programs (Adobe, Java...): the program checks for updates when it opens. The last rule: anything more specific wins.
